sectorSummary.overview: All six lenders reported sequential AUM growth and continued earnings recovery, supported by collections, operating leverage and more selective lending. Weather-related collection risks remain prominent, while guidance diverges: CreditAccess raised profitability ranges and Fusion deferred the timing of its ₹10,000 Cr ambition.

trends.text: Loan books expanded sequentially as lenders balanced growth with tighter borrower selection and collection discipline.
Improved collection performance and lower reported NPAs supported recovery, with definitions and the effect of portfolio sales requiring company-specific review.

tailwinds.text: Operating leverage, better branch productivity or cost controls supported margins and earnings.
Lower borrowing costs were reported as funding access and lender confidence improved.

headwinds.text: Drought, flooding or rainfall disruption prompted close regional monitoring; stable current collections do not settle the eventual credit-cost impact.
Growth delivery still depends on a stronger H2 or improved disbursement momentum, despite better current profitability.

opportunities.text: Individual borrower graduation and non-JLG lending can deepen existing customer relationships without proportionate branch investment.
Secured MSME, housing and gold products offer diversification beyond core group microfinance.

risks.text: Arman said loans originated from April 2026 lacked CGFMU cover pending scheme renewal; timing and final terms remained uncertain.
ARC sales contributed to reported asset-quality improvement at Fusion and Spandana, so headline NPA reductions need to be assessed alongside recoveries and credit costs.

insights.text: CreditAccess raised FY27 ROA guidance to 5.2–5.8%, ROE to 21–24% and NIM to 14.4–14.7%, while retaining 20–25% AUM growth.
Fusion’s ₹10,000 Cr AUM goal is now an undated medium-term ambition; Spandana separately reiterated its March 2028 aspiration.
Satin retained 20–25% FY27 AUM growth and is building buffers; its 31% YoY September growth should not be confused with 9% growth from the start of FY27.
